units.translation: ⟦1⟧ i.e. ⟦2⟧ requires the opposite ⟦3⟧ (Hermann) and not ⟦4⟧ “on earth”; the same corruption is at 838, 871. ⟦5⟧ also ⟦6⟧. ⟦7⟧, the envious one, disturbing his happiness; no other emendation of the transmitted ⟦8⟧ seems to offer itself, and there is also a certain analogy of sense to ⟦9⟧. But what the ⟦10⟧ is, not a dance around him, but rather upon him, and why ⟦11⟧, is clarified by the following antistrophe ⟦12⟧.

Already Heath and after him Hermann, Dindorf and others transposed this, before 368, so that it now simply becomes part of antistrophe β; but if in this way the form also becomes regular, the sense still suffers.

⟦1⟧ “for in truth (⟦2⟧. 674. Frg. 308) with mighty leap” etc. has no connection at all with ⟦3⟧; on the other hand, with ⟦4⟧ the very closest, as also especially ⟦5⟧ refers back to ⟦6⟧ 371, and likewise antistrophe ⟦7⟧ is now connected, whereas the connection with ⟦8⟧ is deficient: how can he fall over from dancing? What kind of dance that is must first be described, and in general after the next description in antistrophe ⟦9⟧ the ⟦10⟧. ⟦11⟧ sounds quite feeble. — The hiatus after ⟦12⟧ shows the break of synaphea here; therefore one must not write in tetrameters. ⟦13⟧ is explained in the scholia in two ways: ⟦14⟧, and ⟦15⟧ (with a new sentence) ⟦16⟧. Since in the latter way ⟦17⟧ cannot be construed, except if one makes ⟦18⟧ . . ⟦19⟧ a parenthesis, and even so only with harshness, I prefer the former: ⟦20⟧ therefore active, which it can be as well as passive.
with envious dances of the foot
causing stumbling to the swift-running limbs
bringing my stumbling limbs upon their swift-running limbs
and for the swift-running their limbs become stumbling because of the grievous ruin coming upon them from me
⟦1⟧ before ⟦2⟧. can be inferred from the second scholion, although not with certainty as an actual reading; in the other interpretation one wrote 〈⟦3⟧〉 (Hermann).

⟦1⟧ connects with the Homeric ⟦2⟧, Ψ 375; so even if he wants to run away, we bring him down in his course. The image of fleeing and pursuing (75 ff., 137 ff., etc.) is, however, used only here and is immediately (377 ⟦3⟧.) imperceptibly abandoned again.
falling, he does not know, etc.
